edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Milk is plausibly linked to Colorectal cancer through mechanisms that fit its exposure class and target tissue, but the exact pathway depends on dose, timing, and baseline vulnerability. The best interpretation is usually that it changes the biologic setting in which Colorectal cancer develops rather than acting as a single on-off switch.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link milk to lower risk of colorectal cancer in general adult. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
